1137214074:
Dael is a perfumer with a traveler’s heart. He hopes to carry Bloomville’s signature fragrances across the world and share them wherever the road takes him.
After his family passed away, he began living on the move.
Whenever his travels brought him near the Foresta delle Stelle cadenti, he would visit there instead of returning to Bloomville, because to him, the Celestis were the last family he had left.
It all began with a simple joke.
Once, when Dael was little, he asked his mother where he came from.
She brought him to the Celestis outpost and told him she had found him there and carried him home.
"So you were a little Celestis," she said. "You only look like this because I brought you back to Bloomville."
Young Dael believed every word.
From then on, he was always running off to the Celestis outpost to play.
He thought of the Celestis as his family, and eventually he could almost understand their language.
After growing up, Dael knew it had only been his mother’s little joke. Still, the Celestis at the outpost never stopped feeling special to him.
When he is far from home, he misses them.
But when he is close by, it is enough simply to know they are safe.

By the time the Icho had already claimed his name, he was still just an Emberpup, training day after day, staring up at the blooming Thousand-Fang Ridge. His growth was slow—so slow it went unnoticed, even dismissed as ordinary. Many Flameruffs and Emberpups pitied him, saying it was unfortunate to be born in the same age as the Icho. Yet while others sighed, he kept moving forward at his own pace. Step by step, year after year, he eventually reached the same height the Icho had once attained.
"I’m not talented."
"If I have any talent at all... it’s that I never stopped."

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has been unusually active in some regions lately, causing special changes in the local ecosystem.
2. During the event, in the first 3 Nurture runs you do each weekend in the designated area, the chance for Stadio Nova Aniimo to appear will greatly increase. After harvesting Veinfruit, your area Prismana gain is boosted by an additional 50 %.
Doing Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy. When you capture Aniimo, you also have a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, which increases the region’s Prismatic Energy.
Each time the area’s Prismatic Energy increases through Nurture, there is a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, attracting local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
Each time you capture an Aniimo and trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, attracting local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Head there to explore and capture them.
4. During the event, some special Prismana Aniimo will also be drawn by Vein energy and appear for a limited time in designated areas. Check the event schedule below for which Prismana Aniimo appear in each phase and where.

<Twenty>
I spent my twentieth birthday with Tucker.
It was a rare sunny day in the Boschi Nebbiosi, and we met up at <style=Hint_BgD>our old spot</style>.
Tucker always liked burying himself there, and no one but me could ever call him out.
We had agreed long in advance that we’d celebrate together today.
Everyone in the Boschi Nebbiosi, feel the power of our “Magic Sound Duet”!
...
The Witchins who had gathered for a music party all covered their ears and ran off.
Our magic sound is more powerful than theirs, hands down!
...
Even the Pomeggs, who love a good bit of noise, ran off.
...
Looking around, there wasn’t a single Hummin left.
...
Sure enough, we made everyone in the Boschi Nebbiosi hear our singing!
Although no one could tell we were singing the “Birthday Song.”
...
I never used to like singing the birthday song, nor celebrating birthdays.
Because I’ve been off-key since I was little, and everyone always laughed at me.
But singing together with Tucker, even if the whole Boschi Nebbiosi can’t stand it, I’m happy.
I’m starting to look forward to my next birthday.
The next birthday, and the one after, and the one after that... I want to spend them all with Tucker!

When the Alpha Irisal was still an Iris, the former Alpha left it with a kid from Bloomville. The kid’s name was Clovis, a florist of Bloomville, born with a special perception of life. They became partners—the Irisal’s job was to dance on the flower fields to help them grow while Clovis perceived the status of each plant in order to make proper plans for cultivating them.
It was just another day, Clovis suddenly gave it a hair band. It turns out that a couple of days before, Clovis was given an urgent order, so he had to ask two other Irises for help and treated them with lots of nectar. But Clovis didn’t forget about his good friend. Floret did not know why it felt so sad, but Clovis noticed. He told it the prettiest hair band was for his best friend, Floret, and there was only one like it in the world.
Since Floret evolved into an Irisal, it also grew out of the hair band. But it still carries it wherever it goes.

1. Each of an Aniimo’s six attributes has [Innate Potential] and [Acquired Potential].
<style=Hint_BgL>[Innate Potential]</style> is fixed at birth and can only be increased through special methods, such as Capafruit.
<style=Hint_BgL>[Acquired Potential]</style> can be raised through Capability Awakening. More items of higher rarity are required for later increases.
The <style=Hint_BgL>sum of Innate Potential and Acquired Potential</style> cannot exceed <style=Hint_BgL>20</style>. Higher Potential results in greater stat increases as the Aniimo levels up.
2. The number of Capability Awakenings available to an Aniimo can be increased by reaching specific Resonance Star Ranks and leveling up.

Just as I expected, I lost another report.
I accidentally ran into a Fenrier while it was challenging a powerful opponent, so I had to run.
But it’s fine, I have more new findings this time!
————
Almost all Fenriers wish to be more powerful, so they keep challenging each other and get hurt a lot.
Fenriers can strengthen their willpower through constant fighting and finally find an opportunity to evolve into a Glynsera.
I helped a Fenrier treat its wound and it gave me some new information.
It turns out that within the Bonesky family, the most powerful Glynsera gets to earn the name Recas.
It sounds more like a title than a name to me.
————
This research trip went really well!
It took me some effort but I finally got to twine with a young Bonesky and learned about the legend of Recas from an elder of the family.
I must write it down!
...Oops, the note is full.

1. During the event, Polaris Institute will publish an Ecological Investigation. Each investigation focuses on a single ecological theme and selects a range of representative Aniimo as investigation targets.
2. Pathfinders must follow the investigation list and catch the corresponding Aniimo to help the Institute complete its ecological investigation and earn Investigation Points.
3. Each target Aniimo only grants points the first time its investigation is completed. Catching the same target again will not grant additional points.
4. Please pay close attention to Aniimo forms. Only catching an Aniimo in the same form as listed on the investigation list will complete the corresponding investigation.
5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.
6. If the investigation target is an Aniimo the Pathfinder has not yet registered in the Aniilog, the points earned for completing its investigation for the first time will be doubled.

One Baleetle found a perfect stone, but failed to push it over the mountain and bring it back. Every time it neared the peak, the ball rolled back down, dragging the Baleetle with it. Over time, this created a strange, straight path up the mountain. One day, the earth shook, the mountain crumbled, and a stone wall marked with the words "mountain path" fell onto Berylline Vale, which was the only proof of this event. Later, other Baleetles saw this "mountain path" and used it as a natural racetrack. Years later, the rock turned pure cyan, nurturing a stoneflower within—a symbol of life blooming in the wrong place.

1. This game is a role-playing game suitable for users aged 12 and above. It is recommended that minors use this game under parental supervision.
2. This game is based on a fictional Lore. The Story tells of Pathfinders forming friendships with creatures from a fictional World and exploring adventures together in a new World. The plot is Easy and positive, with no adaptations based on real history or the real World. The scenes are bright and colorful, with upbeat and lively music. Pathfinders play as human Pathfinders in the game. Gameplay is based on physical operations of moderate difficulty and cognitive judgment of moderate difficulty, encouraging Pathfinders to achieve their goals through thinking and Training. The game includes a text and voice-based stranger social System.
3. This game has a real-name authentication System. Users authenticated as minors will be subject to the following restrictions: minor users may only log in to the game from 20:00 to 21:00 on Fridays, Saturdays, Sols, and legal holidays. They are not allowed to play at other times.
4. This game focuses on exploration and Training, and can cultivate Pathfinders' imagination and love for nature. In the game, every Pathfinder can form deep friendships with adorable fictional creatures and embark on a journey of Talents together, exploring unknown territories. During this process, Pathfinders will not only experience adventures, but also enjoy the joy of teamwork. The game design can bring optimistic and positive emotional responses to Pathfinders, guide Pathfinders to form positive emotional expressions, and gain a relaxed and comfortable emotional experience.

1218400877:
Day Eleven
This has to be the most unbelievable scene I’ve witnessed in my entire life.
An enormous Echoback showed up in the storm and guided its struggling brothers and sisters back into the depths of the sea, one by one.
Its powerful singing even drowned out the howling winds and thunder. It just kept singing until all the stranded Echobacks found their way back.
Watching its figure swimming through the waves, I realized that no storm lasts forever. 
Just like every storm I’ve been through, they always end with blue skies.

Day Fifteen
The storm has finally stopped.
I didn’t fail my reputation as an old sailor, just like the Echoback didn’t fail its brothers and sisters.
It brought them all back to the sea, but stayed behind... forever, on this shore.
The raft I made was too small to tow it, so I carved its tale into this stone.
I know that its bones will stand here for a very long time.

May its story be told for eternity.
May all sailors finally see their blue skies.

1242069596:
Icho was born in Beast Fang Ridge, long ago.
It did not take long for it to become the strongest Emberpup. Then the strongest Flameruff. Then, the strongest Scorchhowl that Beast Fang Ridge had ever known. The name Icho had always belonged to the strongest of each generation, but this one came to be known as the Icho among Icho.
There was a fire inside it that never seemed to go out. That fire made it crave battle, crave something that could make it burn brighter. Back then, the only thing it cared about was finding someone with harder fists. Everything else? It barely saw it. It only wanted to grow stronger, stronger, and stronger still.
Every fighter in Beast Fang Ridge was just another opponent waiting to fall.
————
Then, one day, there were no opponents left.
It had fought everyone worth fighting and beaten everyone worth beating. Victory came too easily. Battle lost its fun. Standing in the middle of the Thousand-Fang Ridge, staring at the withered Ridgeback Trees, it suddenly felt... empty.
It had lost its rivals. It had lost its goal. The fire still burned inside it, but it had nowhere to go.
Those were lonely days.
————
Then an outsider appeared.
His name was Lewis. They did not share a language, so ordinary words were useless. But Lewis was clever. He discovered that fists spoke well enough.
They fought ninety-nine times. Icho lost ninety-nine times.
Badly. Again and again. But Icho was not bitter. If anything, the dying fire inside it began to burn again.
"Want to come with me?" Lewis asked after every victory. "You will become stronger."
On the ninety-ninth defeat, Icho said, "Yes."
It did not yield because it had lost. It yielded because it had finally found someone whose fists were harder than its own. It wanted to know how far it could go by following him.
————
Only after leaving Beast Fang Ridge did Icho begin to understand something.
Winning was not the end.
As a child, it carved its path with its fists. As a young fighter, it claimed the title of strongest among them. Later, those fists became the way it understood the world. After all this time, the one thing that has never changed is that Icho still trusts its fists.
It has lost plenty along the way: the fire of youth, its rivals, even the title of strongest. But it is not alone.
Maybe because that man is still standing across from it. Maybe because clenching its fists still feels exactly the same.
————
These days, Icho rarely leaves Lewis’s side.
Not because Icho has grown weaker, but because Lewis has changed. The man who once defeated it ninety-nine times with his fists is now gravely injured, and has even lost the ability to Twine with Icho. What happened to Lewis? Icho does not know. Neither do you.
But Icho knows one thing for certain.
Lewis has not lost his fighting spirit. And neither has Icho.
There will be no hundredth fight between them. Not because they no longer want one, but because some things matter more than winning. Icho once thought fists existed to defeat opponents. Now it understands: fists are what carry you to the next battle, and what help you find someone willing to stand beside you when it comes.
The Thousand-Fang Ridge once bloomed for Icho. They once bloomed for the Inferlupa as well.
Icho knows the flame will never go out. And it will not burn in the Thousand-Fang Ridge alone.

My dear book buddy Clovis, as an Aniimo researcher myself, I feel obliged to remind you that keeping a Budclaw is not an easy thing to do... Actually, it’s not easy to keep any Aniimo.

First of all, there’s something you need to know about Budclaws.
1. Heartblooms
Heartblooms, the small buds on top of each Budclaw’s head, are parasitic entities present from birth. They provide nutrients for their host through photosynthesis. That’s why Budclaws are diurnal and enjoy sunbathing so much—it keeps them healthy.

2. Lifetime Partners
Budclaws are highly faithful Aniimo—they have only one partner for life.
The heartblooms on their heads (those small buds) reflect how close they are to their mates.
That means if you ever find a flower on your Budclaw buddy’s head, congratulations! You’ll soon have a couple of Budclaws and probably many baby Budclaws in the future.
Also, if a Budclaw has a flower on its head, other would-be mates will instinctively keep their distance.

Second, you must interact with your Budclaw buddy in the correct way.
- You should never maltreat it (which I believe you’d never do).
- Make sure you’re there for it and comfort it when it feels down (they are usually not that hard to cheer up).
- If a Budclaw ever buries itself deep into the soil, that’s a serious sign—it could be depressed, and you must intervene immediately.

I’m leaving Bloomville to go to the Sea of Flowers mudflats. I was told that there are magical Bulblies there.
I really enjoyed my time at your home, and will remember the stories of heroes we shared so fondly.
I only chose to leave at night to ease the weight of our farewell.
But we’ll see each other again.

Aniimo Researcher Sayn, a friend you spent three days with

Aniimo Transmog Guide
Transmog parts include: Color, Wings, Body, Headwear, and Effects.
Use the items <color=#e49b43>Radiant Dreamshadow</color> and <color=#b767e1>Glimmering Driftshadow</color> to change your Aniimo’s appearance.
<color=#b767e1>Glimmering Driftshadow</color> has the following restrictions:
It can only transmog certain parts, cannot be used while parts are locked, and does not increase Transmog Progress for restricted parts or any parts unlocked afterward.
If you own both items, <color=#b767e1>Glimmering Driftshadow</color> will be consumed first whenever its conditions are met.

Transmog Rates
Part qualities include: <color=#4c94e9>Rare</color>, <color=#b767e1>Epic</color>, and <color=#e49b43>Legendary</color>.
Appearance rates:
<color=#4c94e9>Rare: 77.42%</color>
<color=#b767e1>Epic: 19.36%</color>
<color=#e49b43>Legendary: 3.22%</color>

A <color=#e49b43>Legendary</color> part is guaranteed within 62 attempts.

Part Locking
You can lock up to 3 parts.
The more parts you lock, the more items are consumed.
When parts are locked, consuming more items increases the bonus transmog chance and speeds up Progress growth.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

Okay, I lost the last report again.
But it’s fine, I have a new finding this time!
I believe that my luck has begun to turn! If it weren’t for those who chased me into such a remote corner, I wouldn’t have stumbled onto this gossip.
No, matters of Aniimology can’t be called gossip. This is intelligence!
————
It turns out that the Bonesky and Emberpup families have been fighting each other for control of Beast Fang Ridge.
However, it’s not all hostile between them—some Boneskies and Emberpups are secretly friends.
It’s worth noting that Boneskies and Emberpups once coexisted peacefully and had a simple partnership—
Boneskies would create ice pillars, while Emberpups would melt them with fire to get fresh water in the caverns.
What’s more, stronger Emberpups would thaw the surface of the underground river with fire, whereas stronger Boneskies would absorb the biting cold air in the cave to prevent the Emberpups coming to fetch water from getting frostbite.
This partnership, however, has long become a thing of the past.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

1324459152:
In Awen’s childhood memories, her home was just like any ordinary family home in Bloomville — simple, warm, and familiar. Back then, the biggest problem in her life seemed to be that her mother would stay out in the flower fields to cultivate new varieties instead of coming home, while her father’s complaints gave Awen no end of headaches.
Even when she sensed that she was somehow different from the other people of Bloomville, it never troubled her back then.
Except on those rare occasions when snow fell over the Sea of Flowers.
Her mother would gaze toward its deepest reaches, a wistful look in her eyes.
Young Awen asked her mother what lay beyond the Sea of Flowers.
Her mother only shook her head, as if there were things she couldn’t bring herself to speak about.
When Awen grew up, she found a line in her mother’s research notes — no context before it, none after.
"It’s snowing, but my homeland isn’t there anymore."
It was then that Awen understood — no wonder she carried a different scent from the people of Bloomville. She had another homeland somewhere.
She wanted to find that homeland, to find the "origin" she had never visited.
At last, after braving countless dangers, she reached the ancient white perfume tower deep within the Sea of Flowers, and found the perfume formula called "Homeland" — and with it, her origin.
She was from Azureville. She had never truly belonged here.
She thought: she had to leave this place and go toward her origin.
As for the perfume named "Homeland" — there was no need to bring it to her mother. Because the homeland in her mother’s heart was the white plateau, collapsed utterly in the upheaval of the earth — the place where she had lived alongside the Budsquires in her own childhood.
For some people, home is a guiding scent, leading toward the place they came from.
For others, home is a place one is destined to leave. To leave home is to begin anew.

Among the Budsquire family, Thornblades are guardians armed with unbreakable thorns.
To protect his little sister, one Budsquire brother became a mighty Thornblade. He challenged one famed Lethal Thorn after another, making the same pact each time: the loser would break off their own thorn.
But no Thornblade wins forever.
After his thorn was broken, he could not bear to be comforted by his sister, much less protected by her. So he ventured into a thunderstorm, hoping to become a stronger Thunderstorm Thornblade.
He failed.
After losing her brother, the little sister was no longer the innocent flower she once was. When her tears finally ran dry, she began her own training.
On a stormy night, she bloomed into a flower of grief, with thorns as cold and merciless as her pain.
Since then, she has cut down every challenger without hesitation, breaking their thorns without mercy.
Perhaps because that same cruel ritual took her brother from her. Perhaps because she despises the duels themselves.
Or perhaps she is still waiting for someone strong enough to defeat her—to take the Pale Thorn from her, and with it, finally set her free.

5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.

1. During the event, you can get Sparks through the following ways:
· Complete the Fire Companion Codex quest.
· Take part in the Continuing Sparks mode.
· Check in at the Co-Raise Sprite "Sparkelf" statue in Horizon Square (only once per day).
2. Continuing Sparks mode details:
· Each day, interact with friends to light up Sparks. Interactions include:
※ Chat: send messages to each other.
※ Party Up: form a team.
※ Gift: send gifts to each other.
※ Aniimo Exchange: exchange Aniimo.
※ Visit Home: visit each other.
· After you light up a Spark, a Spark icon will appear next to your friend’s nickname. The number next to it shows how many days you and that friend have interacted during the event. Once you hit 5 days or more, the Spark icon will also level up.
· The Spark icon will gray out after the daily server refresh at 04:00. Interact with your friends to light it up again.
3. Event rewards:
· When your personal total number of Sparks reaches the required amount, you can claim personal progress rewards.
· When the server-wide total number of Sparks reaches the required amount, all players can claim server-wide progress rewards.
· Special Notes:
※ The Co-Raise Sprite "Sparkelf" with the \<style=Hint\_BgL>Sparkling Mutation\</style> (including the Basic Form and Prismana Form) has a sparkling outline effect, but no partial recolor effect.
※ The Co-Raise Sprite "Sparkelf" (Prismana Form) will be unavailable after the event ends. Please stay tuned for future official announcements.

Unusual signs of Legendary Aniimo have begun appearing everywhere.
The Institute is recruiting Pathfinders to go investigate, and bring back valuable photos and complete the field notes.
Event Details
1. During the event, the Institute will unlock multiple investigation areas over time.
2. Each area has different investigation objectives and environmental features. Dispatch suitable Aniimo to explore them.
3. After completing an investigation, you can obtain the corresponding area rewards and may also receive an extra Chance Encounter Gift.
Investigation Rules
1. Each investigation requires at least 2 Aniimo. You must designate 1 as the Leader Aniimo before the investigation.
2. After the investigation is complete, you will receive base rewards according to the dispatched Aniimo.
Dispatching Aniimo meeting the area preference conditions increases your reward rating.
3. Prismana Form and Sparkling Aniimo can sense the residual energy of Legendary Aniimo, which will help speed up the investigation.

Chance Encounter Gifts
When passing through an area with Legendary Aniimo, something special might appear from their energy.
After completing an investigation, you also have a chance to receive 1 Chance Encounter Reward. One of the following rewards will be granted at random:
- <style=Q_5>Random Leader Aniimo Potential +1</style>
- Starcryst Essence x1
- Capaseed x5
- Vein Essence x1
※ <style=Q_5>The "Random Leader Aniimo Potential +1" effect can only be obtained once in each Aniimo’s lifetime.</style>
※ Aniimo with max Potential cannot obtain the "Random Leader Aniimo Potential +1" effect.

Chapter 5: Flowers and Thorns
The earth trembled, and flowers withered.
With the loss of the whitesnow rose and Cubbo’s roses, the forest descended into chaos and violence.
All the Cubbos and Grizbos woke up.
They roared and rampaged through the forest. Peace was no more.
...
The Bloomville villagers fled from Rosetower Woods.
They brought some Budsquire refugees with them.
To ensure the survival of Budsquires in the world, Princess Melloblum entrusted the care of the Budsquires to Bloomville.
...
Armand did not retreat with the Bloomville villagers.
He was the First Lethal Thorn of the Seven Lethal Thorns! How could he abandon Princess Melloblum?
But he could only watch, helpless, as his companions fell one by one in the onslaught. He hated how powerless he was.
It was then that Princess Melloblum said to him, "Armand, rest now, you’ve done well."
He watched as Princess Melloblum performed that familiar Dance of Blissful Bloom.
The dance gave the Budsquires enough strength to retreat into the Maze of Thorns.
After entrusting her daughter, the little princess, to Armand, Princess Melloblum fell at last.
————

<style=Hint_BgL>[Acquired Potential]</style> can be increased through Capability Awakening. The more times it is increased, the more and rarer items are required.

1. During the event, Polaris Institute will publish an Ecological Investigation. Each investigation focuses on a single ecological theme and selects a range of representative Aniimo as investigation targets.
2. Pathfinders must follow the investigation list and catch the corresponding Aniimo to help the Institute complete its ecological investigation and earn Investigation Points.
3. Each target Aniimo only grants points the first time its investigation is completed. Catching the same target again will not grant additional points.
4. Please pay close attention to Aniimo forms. Only catching an Aniimo in the same form as listed on the investigation list will complete the corresponding investigation.
5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.
6. If the investigation target is an Aniimo the Pathfinder has not yet registered in the Aniilog, the points earned for completing its investigation for the first time will be doubled.

3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.

1431258841:
Cinderclaw was once an Omega Flameruff of an Emberpup family.
In his youth, he was the flashiest Emberpup around. Every day, he chased the old Omega’s tail and challenged him, getting a mouthful of mud every time he fell, only to climb back up again. Then one day, he finally won. The old Omega gave him one last look, then turned and walked down from the peak.
"I won," Cinderclaw told himself. "I am the strongest now."
But he soon learned that becoming the strongest was not the end. It meant more challenges.
Young Emberpups challenged him one after another, each trying to prove they were stronger than the Omega. Cinderclaw defeated them again and again, but every victory left him a little more tired.
"Am I getting old?" Cinderclaw began to ask himself.
His flame still burned bright. His strength was still mighty. But his heart had begun to age. He started to fear defeat, not because of defeat itself, but because defeat would mean, "I am old. I cannot do this anymore."
That feeling reached its peak on the day he was defeated by a young Emberpup.
That day, Cinderclaw lay on the ground and looked up at the young Flameruff standing before him, eyes full of hunger for victory. Cinderclaw remembered himself from long ago, the Emberpup who would not stop chasing the old Omega’s tail.
"I lost," Cinderclaw said. "The Omega’s place is yours now."
He felt a wave of relief, followed by a crushing sense of loss. He did not know what else he could do. He had been the Omega for too long, grown too used to the pack looking up to him, and forgotten how to be an ordinary wolf.
"Maybe I should go to Thousand-Fang Ridge," Cinderclaw told himself. "Now that I have set down the burden of being Omega, maybe... I should go wild one last time."
He challenged Icho.
Then, everything ended.
With a single strike, Icho knocked Cinderclaw down. Cinderclaw lay on the ground of Thousand-Fang Ridge, gazed at the withered Ridgeback Trees, and suddenly laughed.
"I really am too old," he said. "So old I do not even have the strength to stand."
But after he fell, something he never expected happened. A legend began to spread across Beast Fang Ridge: the "Immortal Warrior."
They say that after the defeated old Omega left the peak, he still left his footprints all across Beast Fang Ridge. He taught young Emberpups how to fight, helped injured Emberpups find their way home, and even drove off an entire Bonesky family alone during one raid.
"He did not grow old. He just found another way to fight," said the Emberpups he had helped.
But Cinderclaw did not know any of this. He was trapped in Thousand-Fang Ridge and became an Inferlupa. Around his feet was a chain called "old age," and over his heart lay a layer of dust called "powerlessness."
"I am too old," Cinderclaw told himself. "Too old to do anything."
But he did not know that beneath the peak, flames can still burn. Leaving the summit may not be the end. It may be the beginning of passing on the torch.

I found a strange Celestis.
What made it strange was that it seemed smarter than the others.
It would sharpen stones, cut through the thick skin of a large Starine, and enjoy the treat inside.

Was it smart enough to eat large Starines? Or did eating large Starines make it smarter?
----
A colorful large Starine grew on the large Starine Tree. Very unusual.
Most importantly, BINI detected Lumin energy from it. It may contain some Vein power.
I need to find a chance to steal that colorful large Starine.

Too late. That strange Celestis ate it.
An hour later, in a flash of light, the strange Celestis evolved into a Prismana Form Stellarys.
It seems the Prismana Form of Aniimo is closely tied to Vein power.

Unusual signs of Legendary Aniimo have begun appearing everywhere.
The Institute is recruiting Pathfinders to go investigate, and bring back valuable photos and complete the field notes.
Event Details
1. During the event, the Institute will unlock multiple investigation areas over time.
2. Each area has different investigation objectives and environmental features. Dispatch suitable Aniimo to explore them.
3. After completing an investigation, you can obtain the corresponding area rewards and may also receive an extra Chance Encounter Gift.
Investigation Rules
1. Each investigation requires at least 2 Aniimo. You must designate 1 as the Leader Aniimo before the investigation.
2. After the investigation is complete, you will receive base rewards according to the dispatched Aniimo.
Dispatching Aniimo meeting the area preference conditions increases your reward rating.
3. Prismana Form and Sparkling Aniimo can sense the residual energy of Legendary Aniimo, which will help speed up the investigation.

Chance Encounter Gifts
When passing through an area with Legendary Aniimo, something special might appear from their energy.
After completing an investigation, you also have a chance to receive 1 Chance Encounter Reward. One of the following rewards will be granted at random:

1518454137:
Decades ago, the Pianure Ventose lost their peaceful, tranquil nature. The frequent shifts of the world and ceaseless conflict defined these plains from then on.
It’s said that dangerous creatures, even those pesky Sparkis, formed mobs at night and sneaked into Bloomville.
As such, besides perfumers, many in Bloomville had also become night watchers.
————
One night, Night Watcher Reikito was feeling down, her stomach growling with hunger.
As she passed by Grace’s house, she discovered that she had left a pan of honey cakes out for night watchers to enjoy, free of charge. But she was conflicted.
Although she would be able to sate her appetite, Night Watcher Reikito was worried that the taste might knock her out on the spot.
It was right at this time that the sound of a beastly howl filled her ears.
Night Watcher Reikito hurried to grasp her sword as she looked to the sky.
It was the Infergon!
Reikito pulled out her old rusty iron sword that was the butt of many a joke, as her eyes locked on the Infergon. At the same time, she shouted for the townsfolk to flee.
In the blink of an eye, the Infergon descended before Reikito.
Reikito was like a speck in comparison to the Infergon’s gargantuan size.
But Reikito still defended her people and confronted the mighty Infergon.
No one expected what happened next. The Infergon did not destroy any houses. It did not harm anyone. Instead, it stared at Grace’s stove... and drooled.
————
The Infergon left, content, even leaving an unusual red rose behind.
Grace’s family was elated.
As perfumers, they knew that this was the start of a legendary perfume.
They began researching day and night, and have now grown accustomed to the Infergon’s occasional nightly visits.
Although now, the townsfolk of Bloomville worry more about the explosions coming from Grace’s abode than they do about the Infergon himself.

1525863141:
At first, Elvira’s ancestor only wanted to create a perfume that captured sorrow.
After her mother passed away, something inside her stayed hollow. It was not pain, exactly. It was cold. It was the silence left behind by footsteps she would never hear again. She tried to bottle that feeling with the depth of sandalwood, the coolness of frankincense, and the airy haze of white musk.
But after three months of trying, she still could not make it. The longing in her heart was too heavy. No fragrance could truly hold it.
One evening, she sat by the sea, lost in thought. Then a song drifted over the water, low and haunting, long and far-reaching, like a greeting carried from another world. Following the sound, she found a lone Echoback gliding through the water.
It kept singing, again and again, as if waiting for an answer that would never come.
With each Echoback Song, luminous pink flowers bloomed along the nearby shore. Their clear, glowing petals slowly unfurled, as though the song itself had taken form. Elvira’s ancestor reached out to touch one. A bead of moisture slipped from the petal, carrying a strange warmth with it.
And in that instant, she remembered her mother’s hand. Not as it was at the end, thin and fragile, but as it had been years ago, warm and gentle, leading her through the flower fields. It carried the scent of Duskwhisper.
Then she understood. The Echoback was not singing out of sorrow. It sang because it still remembered the warmth of the one it had lost. Longing is not cold. It is the glow of a warmth that still endures, even across an immeasurable distance.
And so, Elvira’s ancestor named the flower Whalesong Blossom. She brought it back to Bloomville and used it to craft the very first bottle of "Whisper of Longing."
On the day it was finished, Elvira dabbed it onto her wrist. It was nothing like the deep, cool, elusive scent she had set out to make. Through the haze of its fragrance, she could almost see her mother again, standing in a field of violet blossoms, smiling with the same joy as before.

1529906549:
Zephyro is a perfumer of the mixture school, and also the inheritor of legendary perfumes.
Yet for him, perfume making feels more like a duty than a passion.
Zephyro holds his own, impractical dream—
He wants to fly across the sea.
Fortunately, he can twine with Aniimo.
Unfortunately, he can only twine with Flutternyms.
Without the wind’s aid, a Flutternym cannot fly across the sea.
Luckily, his Flutternym was once the companion of Zephyro’s grandfather, and it knows that singing the Song of Freedom can make the Bell of Freedom bloom.
When the Bell of Freedom blooms, a great wind will rise.
They could then ride that wind across the sea, just as his grandfather once did.
And so, Zephyro and his Flutternym would often sing near the Bell of Freedom.
Yet the Bell did not bloom—not once.
The wind even carried away the Song of Freedom.
They grew almost mad with frustration.
Singing, waiting, and thinking—
Great wind, great wind—when will you come?
Is our song not free enough? Why won’t the Bell of Freedom bloom?
————
When the Bell of Freedom finally bloomed, Zephyro understood:
The freedom to leave and the freedom to stay are one and the same.
Still, he chose to ride the great wind with his Flutternym and left.
Because that was the freedom they desired.
No nobler than staying, only true to their hearts.
————
When the perfume "Freedom’s Breeze" was complete, Zephyro let go of everything at last.
He was no longer a perfumer, and he relinquished the duty passed down through the generations.
He felt light, so light.
For all he carried now was the wish to fly across the sea.
"To you who share this destiny, I give this Freedom’s Breeze—
May it carry you, too, toward the place in your heart."

Dear Pathfinder,

Long time no see! It’s Nicole! How have you been?
I have a secret to tell you. We’re about to get the chance to take part in a <style=Hint_BgL>Special Expedition</style>!
According to the Institute’s latest survey, some unusual signals have appeared near <style=Hint_BgL>Echoback Landing</style>!
Bloomville has also sent word that someone heard <style=Hint_BgL>mysterious sounds</style> along the coast—nothing like anything a human would make!
I think this might just be an <style=Hint_BgL>Aniimo we’ve never seen before</style>!

Dr. Lewis mentioned that the Institute once investigated the deep sea, where it seems to connect to an unknown region.
But it’s always been blocked by some mysterious force, appearing and disappearing like mist. It’s impossible to explore properly.
This time though, I have a strong feeling that we’ll discover the true <style=Hint_BgL>Mysterious Sea</style>!
A new place means new Aniimo! ...I got more and more excited just thinking about it, so I had to tell you right away!
Dr. Lewis is compiling the list of expedition candidates, and the signal may appear very soon.
Until then, let’s get ready together and wait for Dr. Lewis to make contact!

Wishing you all the best!

1577817085:
Perfumers have always been the object of admiration in Bloomville, but Marlowe seemed to be the exception.
Whenever Marlowe promotes a new perfume, everyone keeps their distance, afraid that getting too close might cause them to become another "victim."
Yet there are still those who, swayed by his passionate pitches, end up passing out on the spot.
The elder was deeply troubled by this.
As there was nothing else to be done, the elder made Marlowe stand near his own home to promote his products. That way, whoever was unfortunate enough to fall prey to his concoctions could be dragged back to the elder’s house for timely treatment.
The elder had worn himself out worrying over Marlowe.
In fact, the elder’s favor toward Marlowe was not without reason.
Marlowe was born with a "bad nose," unable to tell one scent from another.
As a child, he tried learning perfume blending like everyone else, and eagerly brought his very first perfume to the elder.
The elder was overwhelmed by the stench, which smelled like "rotten honey cake"... and passed out on the spot.
When he woke up and saw Marlowe watching him with concern, he had no choice but to say he only passed out from delight—the scent was simply too wonderful.
Marlowe was so excited that he decided then that he was a genius perfumer.
And so, even though his perfume promotions continued to meet resistance, he never gave up his pursuit of perfume making.
————
Marlowe’s belief that he was a genius perfumer wasn’t just because of the elder’s compliment.
Though he couldn’t smell the sea breeze or the flowers, he could perceive certain... unusual scents.
For instance, he might catch whiffs of money, freedom, and warmth from people.
He even once caught an Aniimo thief.
Some said Aeolus had closed one door for Marlowe but opened a window.
Others argued it was just Marlowe’s imagination.
Yet when Marlowe crafted "Perfect Mistake," which was later regarded as a legendary perfume, a quiet shift began in people’s minds.
Could he really be a genius? The people of Bloomville started wondering.

1. According to Institute observations, Vein energy has been unusually active in some areas lately, causing special changes in the local ecosystem.
2. During the event, in the first 3 Nurture runs you do each weekend in the designated area, the chance for Stadio Nova Aniimo to appear will greatly increase. After harvesting Veinfruit, your area Prismatic Energy gain is boosted by an additional 50 %.
Doing Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy. When you capture Aniimo, you also have a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, which increases the area’s Prismatic Energy.
Each time the area’s Prismatic Energy increases through Nurture, there is a 3% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, attracting local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
Each time you capture an Aniimo and trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance to trigger a Prismana Flow, attracting local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Head there to explore and capture them.
4. During the event, some special Prismana Aniimo will also be drawn by Vein energy and appear for a limited time in designated areas. Check the event schedule below for which Prismana Aniimo appear in each phase and where.

1594084177:
Blazehowl was the only Flameruff in the Emberpup family to leave behind the legend of "one hundred victories."
He was a lone wolf, without a family or companions, with only a pair of claws that never stayed sheathed and a heart always craving battle.
One hundred victories. One hundred in a row.
That record made Blazehowl an idol to many Emberpups, who told stories of every battle, mimicked every move, and dreamed of one day becoming as strong as him.
But Blazehowl was not happy.
"Winning is too easy," he once told an admiring Emberpup. "I do not want victory. I want the fight itself."
The Emberpup did not understand, only gazing at him with even greater admiration.
Then Icho appeared.
On that day, Blazehowl tasted defeat for the first time. Icho felled him with a single claw.
Blazehowl rose and charged again. Fell. Rose again. Fell again.
In that battle, he lost seven times.
"Impossible," he said, lying on the ground of Thousand-Fang Ridge, staring at the withered Ridgeback Trees. "I should be invincible. I should be the Undefeated Warrior..."
He obsessively challenged Icho. Once, twice, three times... and each challenge ended in defeat. His famed speed meant nothing against Icho, and his crushing strength felt as weak as a breeze.
By the tenth defeat, Blazehowl began to doubt himself.
By the fiftieth defeat, Blazehowl began to fear battle.
By the ninety-ninth defeat, Blazehowl had lost his fighting spirit completely.
On the day of his hundredth defeat, Blazehowl stood at the center of Thousand-Fang Ridge and howled to the sky. It was not a battle cry. It was a wail.
"I lost. I lost completely," he told himself. "I am not the Undefeated Warrior. I am the Hundred-Loss Warrior."
At that moment, a chain appeared around his feet. It was called "fear of failure" and "the inability to accept his imperfect self."
Blazehowl became an Inferlupa.
He no longer challenged anyone, nor did he accept anyone’s challenge. He simply stood in a corner of Thousand-Fang Ridge, silent as a withered tree, cold as stone.
"The Undefeated Warrior is dead," he told every wolf who asked his name. "Now there is only the Hundred-Loss Warrior."
Yet in his heart, a voice still echoed. It was what the admiring Emberpup had said long ago:
"I really, really cannot wait to hear your next victory story!"
Blazehowl closed his eyes. The next victory story... would there ever be one?

1598502496:
In his final moments, Ron looked at the "Beautiful Voice Perfume" and many memories returned to him.
A boy who felt ashamed of his singing met Tucker hiding in a corner, humming an equally off-key tune—and they both stopped feeling sad.
In fact, they began to feel glad, knowing there was "someone else just like me" in the world.
They started singing those awful songs together, louder and louder, more and more joyfully.
And as they sang, their hearts connected, and they gained the power to twine.
"From the moment we twined, we became each other’s greatest friend."
"No matter what happens, that will never change."
————
Ron told this story over and over to his son, again and again, along with the regret of a promise left unfulfilled.
In the end, he set down the perfume and picked up the long-dried glimmer fruit garland.
There was still so much he wanted to say, but by then, he no longer had the strength.
His son held his hand and repeated to him:
"I’ll wear the garland. I’ll find Tucker. I’ll keep your promise for you."
Ron’s consciousness was already fading, drifting in and out with thoughts left unspoken, until he slipped into slumber.
He saw Tucker again, right there before him.
"Tucker, look... I finally made the Beautiful Voice Perfume. Now we can sing together. But now... I almost don’t want to give it to you."
"Sorry... I can’t sing with you anymore. So... will you sing those awful songs alone for me?"
"Don’t wait for me... but don’t forget me, either."
"Just keep singing those off-key tunes... and remember me always."

Pathfinder, welcome to this issue of the Companion Handbook! This issue’s featured Aniimo is <color=#da8000>Fulmintis</color>!
During your adventures out in the world, complete Companion Handbook quests, raise your Companion Handbook level, and earn superb Companion Handbook rewards!

Companion Handbook Editions
The Companion Handbook’s level progress rewards are divided into the Standard Edition and Advanced Edition. The Advanced Edition requires you to unlock the Advanced Companion Handbook. Rewards include 1 <color=#da8000>Prismana Fulmintis</color> with Perfect Potential, a <color=#da8000>Fulminous Soul (an item used to evolve Fulmintis)</color>, and a range of other rewards. It also grants a special perk: Expanded Aniimo storage capacity. The Advanced Edition raises your Aniimo storage capacity by 5, while the Collector’s Edition raises it by 10. These capacity bonuses do not stack; whichever edition you activate last takes priority.
Unlocking the Collector’s Companion Handbook grants additional rewards and perks immediately on top of the Advanced Companion Handbook.

Quests and Companion Handbook EXP
Quests are divided into weekly quests and edition quests. Each quest can only be completed once, and there is no weekly EXP limit.
Weekly quests refresh every Monday at 04:00 (UTC+8), with progress resetting each week. New Seasonal Quests are added to the quest pool every Monday and stay available for the rest of the season. Newly-added quests remain locked until you finish prerequisite quests in their questline. All quests end when the current Companion Handbook ends.
Companion Handbook EXP can also be obtained from Institute Guide - Daily Activity.
Once the Companion Handbook passes Lv.100, it switches to a repeating reward cycle that caps out at Lv.1000.

Gift Details
You can send a gift to friends who meet the required Affinity and have not yet unlocked the Advanced or Collector’s Companion Handbook. They will receive 1 item that can activate either the Advanced or Collector’s Companion Handbook.

Rerun Details
The Prismana Aniimo Egg from this season’s Companion Handbook will return in Season S3, and will be obtainable through Home-related gameplay.

In this world, there are people who are born happy.
Some admire them.
Some find them strange.
Others find them to be quite normal.
Fantine is one of those naturally happy people.
Fantine and Iola are sisters from Bloomville.
The elder sister, Fantine, followed in their father’s footsteps and became a perfumer, while the younger sister, Iola, took after their mother and became a shepherdess.
Fantine couldn’t understand why Iola worried so much over a certain boy named Lycus, and Iola couldn’t understand why Fantine was always so happy.
Iola didn’t just worry about Lycus—she began worrying about Fantine, too.
She wondered if her sister might be ill.
For the first time, Fantine felt a little worried. She took her little Nimbi and went to Driftwise Meadow, hoping to relax a little while searching for perfume ingredients.
Not long after arriving, her Nimbi grew upset.
Holding her upset Nimbi, Fantine felt a sorrow she had never known before, and let the Nimbi go.
She couldn’t understand. Was her joy what made her different? Was being sad really the right way to be?
It wasn’t until the bittersweet bloom blossomed that Fantine suddenly understood.
If Fentufts were happy, and she was happy too, then why shouldn’t a happy Fantine be together with the happy Fentufts?
She even began to wonder—was she actually just a tall, slender Fentuft?

Starry Chrysanthemum
A member of the asteraceae family, this plant has bright green, spoon-shaped leaves. Its slender stems bear flowers about the size of a thumb.
It thrives in well-lit environments and commonly features white, pink, and yellow blossoms.
It’s a tough plant that can survive light trampling by Aniimo,
Making it a good candidate for lawn alternatives.

Millebloom Lotus
A member of the nymphaeaceae family, this aquatic flower has many petals and a splendid appearance. It often grows where Skippies thrive.
Its seeds and roots have a bitter taste and are rarely used in human food, but are highly favored by water Aniimo.
The stems are often made into fragrant sachets during the summer to repel bugs.

Blisswort
A member of the shrub family, it is commonly found on rooftops in the high areas of Bloomville. In spite of the fact that it doesn’t look very pretty, it is the third most popular spice making material in Bloomville.
The perfuma lily itself is tasteless, but the processed juice has a strong fragrance-expanding ability.
A single iris flower combined with perfuma lily juice can emit a scent even richer than a cluster of iris flowers.
It is called perfuma lily because it’s required in the making of almost all types of perfume.

1. During the event, Pathfinders can pick one Prismana Aniimo they like on the event screen. Once your title is promoted to Junior Wayfarer, you can claim the Aniimo you picked. You can change your selection at any time before claiming.
2. The Aniimo you claim will be in Prismana Form, with a randomly generated personality. After you claim it, Phase 2 Prismana Pact will unlock.
3. After Prismana Pact unlocks, Pathfinders can continue collecting Prismana Aniimo within the event’s designated scope. Each time you register a new Prismana Aniimo, it will increase the corresponding Prismana Index completion progress.
4. If the Prismana Aniimo you claimed in Phase 1 is within the Prismana Pact Index scope, it will also count toward your completion progress. Getting the same Prismana Aniimo more than once will not increase progress again.
5. When your Prismana Index completion reaches the required milestones, you can claim the corresponding stage rewards.
6. You can check your current Prismana Aniimo registrations through View Index on the event screen, and keep hunting for Prismana Aniimo you haven’t registered yet.

· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.

1. According to observations by the Institute, Vein energy has been unusually active in some regions recently, causing unusual changes in the local ecosystem.
2. During the event, the chance of Stadio Nova Aniimo appearing will be greatly increased for the first 3 Nurture sessions conducted in the designated area each weekend. After Veinfruit is harvested, the amount of Prismatic Energy gained in the area will receive an additional 50% boost.
Completing Nurture increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy. Capturing Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy.
· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Pathfinders can head there to explore and capture them.
4. During the event, some special Prismana Aniimo will also be drawn by Vein energy and appear in designated areas for a limited time. See the event schedule below for the Prismana Aniimo appearing in each phase and their corresponding areas.

1. During the event, Polaris Institute will publish an Ecological Investigation. Each investigation focuses on a single ecological theme and selects a range of representative Aniimo as investigation targets.
2. Pathfinders must follow the investigation list and catch the corresponding Aniimo to help the Institute complete its ecological investigation and earn Investigation Points.
3. Each target Aniimo only grants points the first time its investigation is completed. Catching the same target again will not grant additional points.
4. Please pay close attention to Aniimo forms. Only catching an Aniimo in the same form as listed on the investigation list will complete the corresponding investigation.
5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.
6. If the investigation target is an Aniimo the Pathfinder has not yet registered in the Aniilog, the points earned for completing its investigation for the first time will be doubled.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

Completing Nurture increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy. Capturing Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy.
· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Pathfinders can head there to explore and capture them.

Even after the Legendary Journey event ends, Pathfinders can still get Irisalis Petals in the following ways (except Tracing the Trail). 

1. Story
Obtain by clearing the following Story chapters: Ceremony Preparations, The Ceremony That Never Began, Colorful Fragrance, The Land of Dancing Illusions, The Land where Dreams Come True, Ancient Sacred Fragrance, Rainbow of the Ground, and A New Journey. 

2. Journey Quests
Obtain by clearing the following Journey Quests: The Legend of Mist and Light, The Legend of Echoback Landing, The Legend of Flowers and Thorns, The Legend of the Land of Falling Stars, The Legend of Thousand-Fang Ridge, The Legend of the Land of Lightning and Thunder, The Legend of Helmuts and Helgons, The Legend of the Bell of Freedom, The Legend of the Berylline Vale, and The Legend of Driftwise Meadow. 

3. Gathering
Follow Irelia’s footsteps and gather Irisalis Petals across Pianure Ventose. 

4. First Alpha Clear
Get them upon your very first victory over the Pianure Ventose Alpha. 

5. Elite Pathfinder Challenges
Obtain by defeating the following elite Pathfinders in Pianure Ventose: Wally, Jilly, Loulla, Aster, Wendell, Cecelia, and Lita. 

6. Branch Nurturing
Obtain by infusing energy into the Pianure Ventose Branch and unlocking its nodes. 

7. Pianure Ventose Silver Badges
Obtain by claiming Silver Badges from each area in Pianure Ventose. 

8. Aniimo Research
Unlock and tap the Stadio Nova Aniimo Index entry inside your Aniilog, complete the research topic Collect Prismana Form, and collect them from rewards. 

9. Tracing the Trail
Obtain from the limited-time event Tracing the Trail.

1738610281:
Graymane was one of the most legendary Flameruffs in his clan. He carried an intoxicating scent of flame, a trace left by countless battles, as if every strand of his fur burned with fighting spirit.
On the day his daughter was born, Graymane stood at the entrance to their den and looked toward Thousand-Fang Ridge in the distance. He made a vow: "Someday, I will make that tree bloom for me. When that day comes, my daughter will know her father is the strongest Scorchhowl."
But Graymane had one fatal flaw. He got lost very, very easily.
Whenever he set out to challenge a powerful foe, only one-twentieth of his time was spent fighting. The rest was spent finding his way. He once took a three-month detour to challenge a Glynsera in the north, only to stumble into a Bonesky family’s territory and send them scattering in fright. He also once chased prey all the way to the edge of Bloomville, where perfumers mistook him for a rare source of fragrance and chased him for three days and nights.
But Graymane never saw it as a problem. "Getting lost is training, too," he always told his daughter. "Every time I lose my way, I meet unexpected opponents and learn unexpected things."
His daughter grew older and slowly got used to her father coming home late. She no longer worried about whether he had been wounded in battle. She worried about whether he had gotten lost at the ends of the world again.
Then one day, Graymane told his daughter, "I am going to Thousand-Fang Ridge. I will earn the Ridgeback Tree’s recognition, just like Icho did. Once I make the Ridgeback Tree bloom for me, I will come home."
Graymane set out.
This time, he did not get lost. He found Thousand-Fang Ridge without a single wrong turn and stood before the withered Ridgeback Trees.
But he failed.
No matter how fiercely his fighting spirit burned, the dead trees gave no response. They stood in silence, as if quietly mocking his weakness.
"Maybe I am still not strong enough," Graymane told himself.
So he waited. He heard that Icho had appeared, and that Thousand-Fang Ridge had bloomed like flame. Graymane saw hope. If Icho could do it, surely he could, too.
He challenged Icho again and again, and lost again and again.
"As long as I become the strongest Scorchhowl, the Ridgeback Tree will recognize me." Graymane clung stubbornly to that belief.
But what he did not know was that the Ridgeback Tree had never bloomed for "the strongest."
Day after day, year after year, Graymane changed from a spirited wolf in his prime into an old wolf with gray-white fur. His fighting spirit wore away with each defeat, and his flame slowly died beneath the withered Ridgeback Tree.
Then one day, Graymane realized he could no longer leave Thousand-Fang Ridge. An invisible chain had appeared around his feet. It was a shackle he had placed on himself, forged from his obsession with "becoming the strongest" and his shame at going home to face his daughter.
He became an Inferlupa.
He no longer got lost, because he had nowhere left to go. Trapped in Thousand-Fang Ridge, he withered alongside the Ridgeback Trees. Sometimes he remembered his daughter, how she chased her own tail in circles when she was little, and the sparkle in her eyes when she asked, "Where did you get lost today, Dad?"
"Home... home..." Graymane the Inferlupa murmured. "Do I still have to keep fighting?"
What he did not know was that his daughter had never blamed him. That little Emberpup still waits outside the dead forest, believing her father is only a "lost fighter" who has not yet found his way home.

1. According to observations by the Institute, Vein energy has been unusually active in some regions recently, causing unusual changes in the local ecosystem.
2. During the event, the chance of Stadio Nova Aniimo appearing will be greatly increased for the first 3 Nurture sessions conducted in the designated area each weekend. After Veinfruit is harvested, the amount of Prismatic Energy gained in the area will receive an additional 50% boost.
Completing Nurture increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy. Capturing Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy.
· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Pathfinders can head there to explore and capture them.

<Age Fifty>
I returned to the Boschi Nebbiosi, but our "old spot" was gone.
Tucker was gone too.
...
Everything had lost its color.
Even the once-noisy, off-key Hummins seemed to have vanished.
...
I stood at the entrance to the maze ruins, almost wishing a crowd of Witchins would make my head spin with their dreadful singing.
But all that remained was silence and desolation.
...
Twenty years ago, I couldn’t wait to say goodbye to my friends and set off for distant lands.
I wanted to escape the shame of my terrible singing.
I dreamed of having a beautiful voice of my own.
And now, as I look at this bottle of "Beautiful Voice Perfume," I miss those days of being surrounded by awful singing more than ever.
...
I lie here, unwilling to leave.
Everything I remember is gone. Only this place, no longer quite our old spot, is still here waiting for me...
No. Tucker is still out there too. He must be waiting for me somewhere.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.

Astra today is nothing near as prosperous, nor as secure, as it looks on the surface. The crises are still very much with us.
...In other words, this is no era for indulging wealthy young people who want to run around doing as they please.
Every one of my decisions carries weight. I would never waste precious resources on my daughter’s whims.
I voted for her simply because I agree with her ideas.
“Wanting a little home to play and roam with Aniimo across the continent of Idyll”...
Honestly, that was my own original vision back when I first adventured across Idyll.
Secretary: Oh? I always thought...
Amber: ...that I was a total pragmatist from the very beginning? Not exactly.
It’s just that Polaris Institute talked me around. The future of Astra, the future of Pathfinders...
They were right. That’s why I started researching mass production of Aniipods, and thankfully, we succeeded.
Secretary: So GoGoHomes is really what you wanted to do all along, but never got the chance?
Amber: Yes. Driving your own little world across the continent of Idyll...
That was the dream I never got to fulfill. But looking at it now, Fannie has fulfilled it in my place.
...I’m glad she’s been able to do it.
As for how far she can take it from here, well, we’ll just have to wait and see.

Perhaps she was influenced by Bloomville’s tea culture, but Princess Melloblum eventually developed a taste for floral tea.
In fact, as more and more Budsquires flocked to her, Princess Melloblum even began hosting tea parties.
The writer, Armand, with his excellent storytelling skills, became a regular guest at these parties.
He also became a link between the Budsquire family and Bloomville’s residents.
...
Bloomville’s perfumers were still working hard to cultivate the miraculous seedlings.
Although they had not yet found success, they had managed to develop a new species of flower, Cubbo’s rose.
The perfumers tasked Armand with delivering some Cubbo’s rose seeds to Princess Melloblum.
...
As the Seven Lethal Thorns dashed through Beardow Woods, Cubbo’s rose seeds were scattered throughout the forest.
Winter passed and spring arrived, and large patches of white blossoms carpeted the forest floor.
They helped the Cubbos drift to sleep.
Gradually, the once dangerous Beardow Woods became safe for the Budsquires as white blossoms covered the wilderness.

Chapter 4: Dance of Blissful Bloom
It was an ordinary spring day when the perfumers of the Florifragrant school guided the miraculous seedling’s vines in a spiral up the white tower.
Bloomville supported the Budsquire family,
and the Budsquires protected the people of Bloomville.
Watching all of this, Armand realized that he had found the true meaning of happiness.
...
These joyful events awakened Princess Melloblum’s long-dormant power.
Among the floating petals and permeating fragrance, she danced a powerful, yet gentle dance.
The dance bathed all the onlookers in happiness, and they all wished to be together forever.
...
It was during this dance that the miraculous seedling finally blossomed.
Perhaps the whitesnow rose is the most beautiful and potent flower in this world?
All the onlookers cheered, and from that day on, Beardow Woods received a new name and became Rosetower Woods.
Only, the whitesnow rose withered at the height of its beauty.

In the <style=Hint_BgL>Capability Awakening</style> system, you can consume Star Dust and other items to <style=Hint_BgL>increase</style> the Aniimo’s <style=Hint_BgL>Acquired Potential</style> for the selected attribute.
1. Each of an Aniimo’s six attributes has [Innate Potential] and [Acquired Potential].
<style=Hint_BgL>[Innate Potential]</style> is fixed at birth and can only be increased through special methods, such as Capafruit.
<style=Hint_BgL>[Acquired Potential]</style> can be raised through Capability Awakening. Higher increases require more, rarer items.
The <style=Hint_BgL>sum of Innate Potential and Acquired Potential</style> cannot exceed <style=Hint_BgL>20</style>. Higher Potential results in greater stat increases as the Aniimo levels up.
2. The number of Capability Awakenings available to an Aniimo depends on its Resonance Star Rank rating, growth stage, and level.

1891484831:
This was once the White Plateau, second in elevation to Twister Peaks, its lands blanketed in deep snow.
Beardow Woods was the only path leading to the White Plateau.
Dangerous Cubbos staggered about, their threatening growls echoing around.
Budsquires shivered as they braved the bitter wind and snow to reach the White Plateau.
For here grew a marvelous flower that had the mysterious power to make Cubbos keep their distance.
Gradually, the people of Bloomville also discovered that white flower.
At first, the Bloomville folk and the Budsquires lived on opposite sides of the flower, leaving each other undisturbed.
Slowly, they began to communicate with each other and live together on the White Plateau.
As the Melloblum performed the Dance of Blissful Bloom, the white flower blossomed against the bitter cold and whirling snow.
It was called the "whitesnow rose"—a miracle on the snow.
The miracle of a beautiful flower blooming amid a harsh and unforgiving world.
And the miracle of the Bloomville folk and Budsquires living together and helping each other.
Where the whitesnow rose grows is a shared homeland of both the Bloomville people and the Budsquire family.

1913204117:
Chapter 1: Princess
Not long ago, the writer and nature lover Armand left Bloomville and ventured deep into the Beardow Woods.
There, he discovered the gentle yet powerful Princess Melloblum, and her six Budsquires.
Imagine his surprise at this discovery, because this area of the forest was known to be home to the ill-tempered Cubbo Family, who did not get along well with others, and tended to force their neighbors off their land.
Upon further observation, Armand noticed a flower seedling growing on the land where Princess Melloblum and her Budsquires lived.
It emitted a faint fragrance, reminiscent of snow, with a lingering scent of joy.
Armand noted that the Cubbo Family seemed reluctant to approach the seedling.
"Lucky," Armand thought, "that nature favors the beautiful."
...
Later, Armand realized that he, too, was blessed by fortune.
Because Budsquires happened to be the only family he could twine with.
After twining with them, he became the seventh Budsquire, devoted to Princess Melloblum.
...
From that day on, the tale of "Princess Melloblum and the Seven Budsquires" began to spread through Beardow Woods.
And Armand enjoyed an idyllic time living in the forest.

1937621481:
The Recas didn’t like being called "Recas"—a title reserved for the strongest of the Bonesky clan. He could never defeat the Icho, not even come close.
Once an ordinary, naive Bonesky, he wandered out of his ice cave one day and got lost, eventually encountering the Icho. He sensed the power radiating from the Icho and grew wary, but the Icho beckoned him over. Having lost his rival, the Icho was lonely and asked, "Little one, do you want to grow stronger?"
Driven by his instinct to challenge the powerful, the Bonesky gave a simple, resolute answer. From that day, the Icho trained him like a master, aiming to raise a worthy opponent. Soon, he grew into a Fenrier.
"Master Icho, how strong must I become?"
"Only more powerful than yesterday. Till you become a Recas and defeat me."
He soon became the Bonesky clan’s mightiest and earned the name Recas, yet he still could not best the Icho. One day, the Icho decided to leave, saying he was no longer the strongest. The Recas couldn’t believe anyone but his future self could surpass the Icho.
"That person comes from beyond our world."
"Now I’m off to test myself in the wider world."
The Recas didn’t understand—only that this "person" had defeated the Icho. So he honed his will, aiming to someday overcome both the Icho and that "person."
Then he became a Glynsera, but he never met "that person."
Then you came along. The moment you defeated the Recas, he finally came to understand.
"I’ve met a person of my own."
"I’ve also seen a bigger world."
