1942515667: The Story of the Bloom Festival
1942586507:
When she was young, Baboni would always ask her mentor Avetine why the legendary perfume formula was called "Golden Wish" and why its main ingredient was named "Golden Answer." Avetine would tell her the story of Haidt, the founding perfumer.
————
Haidt was a genius perfumer, and also a strange one.
She always lived in her own world. Perfumery was her way of speaking to the world, and fragrance was the world’s response.
She could hear others, yet never quite understood them.
It was as if her ears caught the words, but her heart could not truly listen.
In search of inspiration, Haidt came to Blitzwood, where she was struck by lightning and fell unconscious.
After waking up, she found herself in a cave beneath a Blitz Tree. She was brought there by a Blazen. A young, clueless Bolty was also there.
Haidt could not understand them.
Then the Blazen motioned for her to touch its bristling tail.
A faint yet layered current of electricity flowed through her.
Haidt withdrew her hand instinctively, but a word echoed in her heart:
Concern.
She could not understand the word, yet for the first time she felt the meaning of concern.
Injured and touched by this feeling, Haidt stayed—living with the Blazen and its cub.
They grew from strangers into family.
Haidt would often go with the Blazen to the Blitz Tree.
The Blazen would send its wishes to the World of Wonders through electric currents, and would also carry Haidt’s voice into the world.
The thunder rolled on as usual, but nothing ever came of it.
The little Bolty was not interested in this routine, as if it did not believe in the World of Wonders at all.
So the days passed on.
Until one day, the Blazen left—perhaps to the World of Wonders.
Haidt went to the Blitz Tree one last time.
She could not generate electricity, but she cried out from the very bottom of her heart.
A peal of thunder sounded, and a branch fell—like a reply from a distant friend.
————
Young Baboni was deeply drawn to Haidt’s amazing story. She too longed to see that World of Wonders.
Each time, Avetine would shake her head gently and call Baboni her "silly little apprentice."
Baboni grew frustrated.
She began to feel that perhaps Avetine didn’t really like her, especially when Avetine mentioned that once Baboni finished her studies, she would leave for a long journey. Baboni felt sad and was convinced that she just couldn’t wait to leave her foolish apprentice.
It was only when she crafted Golden Wish that Baboni understood—what Avetine truly wished was for Baboni to grow into an apprentice she could trust and finally let go, and that Haidt had not named that fallen branch Golden Answer because the branch itself was extraordinary.
Perhaps that thunder was not truly a reply from her friend Blazen.
But the bond they once shared would never fade.

1965811091:
Day One
I’ve sailed for many years, but never have I faced such a storm surge.
The waves threw me onto the beach like flotsam—what a disgrace to an old sailor like me.
Fortunately, there is enough wild fruit and fresh water near the beach so I don’t need to worry about starving.
I’ll just wait for the storm to die down and then set sail again.

Day Four
I built a shelter to keep me out of the rain—it looks sturdy enough.
I was shocked to see an Echoback stranded on the beach.
It looks young—perhaps the storm messed with its echolocation.
I’ll try to take it back home once the storm stops.

Day Seven
Another shelter destroyed by the storm... That makes three now. The storm shows no sign of stopping.
More and more Echobacks are getting stranded. It’s strange since they almost never get lost at sea.
I can’t even remember how many times their singing has guided me out of storms.
Now we’re trapped on this beach together, and there’s nothing I can do to help them but listen to their wailing all day long in the pouring rain.
I pray to you, Aeolus.
Please help us through the storm and guide us home safely.

Day Ten
I’ve lost another shelter. I’m too tired to build more.
Almighty Aeolus, am I going to die in this foreign land’s endless storm?

Day Eleven
This has to be the most unbelievable scene I’ve witnessed in my entire life.
An enormous Echoback showed up in the storm and guided his struggling brothers and sisters back into the depths of the sea, one by one.
His powerful singing even drowned out the howling winds and thunder. He just kept singing until all the stranded Echobacks found their way back.
Watching his figure swimming through the waves, I realized that no storm lasts forever. 
Just like every storm I’ve been through, they always end with blue skies.

Day Fifteen
The storm has finally stopped.
I didn’t fail my reputation as an old sailor, just like the Echoback didn’t fail his brothers and sisters.
He brought them all back to the sea, but stayed behind... forever, on this shore.
The raft I made was too small to tow him, so I could only carve my journal into this stone.
I know that his bones will stand here for a very long time.

May his life outlast even this story.
May all sailors finally see their blue skies.

1991243920:
My great-grandfather was a musician. In the era when the world lost its color, he inspired people with music.
But music that heals the soul cannot defeat hunger.
He collapsed.
He only came around after a perfumer fed him sweet nectar.
Later, unable to refuse her request, he inherited her legacy and became a perfumer himself.
He felt trapped in a place without wind.
...
Long after, he decided he had had enough and ran all the way to a cliff.
Back then, Argent Strait was still colorless, untouched by the Guardian’s grace like Bloomville.
Crescendo Cliff was ravaged by endless gales, and was known as the "Deadland of a Thousand Winds."
Yet in this deadland, my great-grandfather met some Chirpis singing in the wind.
So they sang loudly together... Even the wind couldn’t take their souls.
They were free.
They sang of freedom.
...
Years later, the Guardian returned green to the land, and Argent Strait revived.
On Crescendo Cliff, my great-grandfather twined with a Chirpi, flying and singing in the fresh wind.
This song gave birth to the Bell of Freedom.
It brought freedom, and a great wind leading to distant places.
...
My great-grandfather passed the perfumer’s legacy to my grandmother.
He was truly free.
They say he rode the great wind to where he wanted to go.
I envy him.
...
If only Flutternyms could fly across the sea.
My partner and I have always thought so.
If only there was a great wind leading far away.
I think, riding that wind, we could find freedom.
...
Now, the wind is here.

3. Once Prismana Pact unlocks, Pathfinders can continue collecting the Prismana Aniimo designated for the event. Registering each new type of Prismana Aniimo increases the corresponding Prismana Index completion.
4. If a Prismana Aniimo claimed in Phase 1 is included in the Prismana Pact Index, it will also count toward completion. Obtaining the same type of Prismana Aniimo more than once will not increase progress again.
5. When Prismana Index completion reaches the specified milestones, the corresponding phase rewards can be claimed.
6. Pathfinders can select View Index on the event screen to check their current Prismana Aniimo registrations and continue searching for any types they have not yet registered.

Soon after, Armand returned to Bloomville to tell his tale of discovery in Beardow Woods.
All who heard his tale were excited about the miraculous seedling.
Especially the perfumers, who wanted to ride the long winds of Aeolus directly to the Beardow Woods and see the miraculous seedling for themselves.
...
The perfumers, fragrant, singing, arrived at the Beardow Woods in high spirits.
They built a towering perfume workshop near the miraculous seedling, and fragrance wafted from the tower.
With the perfumers’ care and nurturing, the miraculous seedling grew amazingly well.
Incredibly, contact with the miraculous seedling’s vines allowed a Budsquire to learn the power of [Thorn].
The Thornblade swore fealty to Princess Melloblum.
A beautiful sentiment and a pure bond were formed.
...
Soon, Princess Melloblum had seven powerful Thornblades in her service.
Yes, not six, but seven Thornblades.
These powerful Aniimo could even fight off the fearsome Grizbo, and became renowned thenceforth in the Budsquire Family as the Seven Lethal Thorns.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

1. Once the event begins, Polaris Institute will reveal this period’s mystery Aniimo silhouette.
2. The initial silhouette will only show the mystery Aniimo’s distinctive features, with the remaining parts hidden. Pathfinders can reveal the hidden parts by photographing Aniimo that share the same features as the mystery Aniimo.
3. Photograph an Aniimo matching the silhouette’s corresponding form and submit it to complete the research topic and claim the corresponding rewards. Successfully photographing before the full silhouette is revealed earns you bonus Aniimo Observation Rewards!
4. Pathfinders can also select photos from their existing album that meet the topic requirements for submission. If a photo contains this period’s mystery Aniimo, it counts toward event completion too.
5. Pay attention to Aniimo forms — only photos where the submitted Aniimo matches the mystery Aniimo’s exact form will count toward event completion.
6. Pathfinders can complete the event by photographing their own Aniimo, other players’ Aniimo, or wild Aniimo on the continent of Idyll.
7. Aniimo in the Holo-Battle Sim are holographic projections, and Aniimo found in Sanctums are bound by ancient seals. Photos taken in these two locations cannot be recognized or submitted.

1. During the event, Polaris Institute will publish an Ecological Investigation List.
2. Pathfinders must follow the investigation list and catch the corresponding Aniimo to help the Institute complete its ecological investigation and earn Investigation Points.
3. Each target Aniimo only grants points the first time its investigation is completed. Catching the same target again will not grant additional points.
4. Please pay close attention to Aniimo forms. Only catching an Aniimo in the same form as listed on the investigation list will complete the corresponding investigation.
5. Once your accumulated Investigation Points reach the specified requirements, you can claim the corresponding milestone rewards.
6. If the investigation target is an Aniimo the Pathfinder has not yet registered in the Aniilog, the points earned for completing its investigation for the first time will be doubled.

2. During the event, the chance of Stadio Nova Aniimo appearing will be greatly increased for the first 3 Nurture sessions conducted in the designated area each weekend. After Veinfruit is harvested, the amount of Prismatic Energy gained in the area will receive an additional 50% boost.
Completing Nurture increases the current area’s Prismatic Energy. Capturing Aniimo also has a chance to trigger a Lucky Strike, increasing the area’s Prismatic Energy.
· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
3. Every weekend, abundant Vein energy will also draw large numbers of Aniimo to gather in the designated area. Pathfinders can head there to explore and capture them.

2099679250:
The First Stop: Bloom Festival
At my first stop in Bloomville, I was lucky enough to participate in the famous Bloom Festival.
A three-day rain of flowers began on the first day of the festival; it was splendid and almost unreal.
The flowers bloomed in the breeze, with petals floating down onto my shoulders and hair, bringing a subtle fragrance. I felt like I was in a fairytale...

The Second Stop: Irisalis
After the festival, I had the privilege of visiting Irisalis, the legendary Aniimo and guardian of Bloomville.
She stood among the flowers, looking intimidating, although the rain of flowers made her a little pale.
According to the locals, she would fall asleep after a show and become vigorous again before the next one.
Like flowers, the cycle of life never stops.
Regrettably, Somniwing, the other powerful Aniimo, didn’t show up. I hope to have the honor of meeting her the next time I come to Bloomville.

The Third Stop: The Sea of Flowers
Today, I visited the Sea of Flowers and tried Bloomville’s special perfume-making art.
The rain of flowers dropped by Irisalis was still ongoing. People picked flowers of different colors and fed them to Dewies. These lovely creatures could transform floral scents into fragrant incense.
I tried the experience myself; the fluffy Dewy in my palm felt so nice and made me realize that mankind and Aniimo can live together in such harmony in Idyll.
I managed to craft a bottle of perfume myself, and after a light sniff, a fresh and delicate fragrance filled my mind, as if all my worries and fatigue were washed away...
Have you ever had such a healing journey?

2101900361:
Just like Cress, Ranka is descended from Bloomville’s night watchers.
But as Irelia restored all the colors to the land, peace settled in, and the night watchers were no longer needed.
People grew eager to explore new lands, searching for ingredients to craft exquisite perfumes.
From this curiosity arose Bloomville’s floral school, devoted to seeking and planting rare flowers—the first perfumery tradition of the town.
Ranka’s ancestor was among its earliest practitioners.
————
Flareburst flowers bloom on the ridgeback trees, radiant symbols of fighting spirit, and were once the very prize the night watchers pursued.
Unlike Cress’s warrior-descended ancestor, Ranka’s forebear carried no rusty iron sword steeped in glory.
Yet he shared the Emberpup’s ambition, climbing toward the highest peaks side by side.
Ever since, perfumers of this lineage have grown alongside their Emberpup companions.
They see flareburst flowers as their goal and regard "true battles" as nourishment on their path of adventure.
————
Ranka, however, did not long for the mightiest path. Even as a perfumer, he was inclined toward idleness.
Perhaps the blood of the night watchers had thinned.
Perhaps it was because his mother once chose the path over him.
Whatever the reason, he preferred lying still in a sunlit meadow of blossoms, breathing in the scents of the flowers.
That was until one day, when the Emberpup he grew up with also left to embark on its own adventure, and a ripple stirred in his heart... soon settling back into calm.
That longing for the path, and that weariness of it, together shaped the Ranka we know today.
And so, whenever he calls himself a "legendary perfumer," it feels both proud and tired.

· Each time Nurture increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 3% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.
· Each time a Lucky Strike triggered while capturing an Aniimo increases the area’s Prismatic Energy, there is a 0.6% chance of triggering a Prismana Flow, causing local Prismana Aniimo to appear.

July 5th
I've ignored you for nearly a week, but nothing has happened here.
Perhaps I should introduce myself to you, my diary. My name is Lycus, and my little brother—a little Emberpup—is called Remy.
I was born on the Grassland, with no friends. The Nimbi flocks always avoid me,
but at least the village elders and my parents are willing to chat with me... and you, my diary.

July 15th
Today was the day to go home and see my parents.
My parents showed a hint of a smile when they saw me. They care for me deeply, but there's always something hidden behind their words.
That night, when I went to wash my hands, I overheard their conversation: "We should tell him the truth. He'll find out sooner or later."
The truth? I don't know what they're referring to, but an inexplicable unease welled up in my Heart.
I returned to my room, saw the diary on the desk, opened a page, and poured this unease onto paper.

July 27th
My parents finally told me the "truth."
It turns out that besides my "adoptive parents" here and my "wolf mother," I have other "parents."
Apparently, they were the parents who gave birth to me.
They seem to have gone to Apeiro... and I'm beginning to have new ideas.

...Praise the guidance of the wind.

With beautiful wings and razor-sharp claws, soaring through the skies.
...
Praise the great and benevolent Aeon, master of gale, time, and the cycles of life.
Its gaze watches over every corner of the Zephyr Coast.
The Grasslands, the ocean, the blazing fire, and that most wondrous of places.
Its power flows through the Veins, and the Veins answer its call.
...
It bestowed the power of Lumin upon the Aniimo, allowing them to grow.
And those Aniimo granted its power shall grow into a form beyond compare.
These are the Guardians.
The Guardians come from this land, protect this land, and love this land.
The Aeon and the Veins grant them strength, and even the Flow bends to their will.
...
Thus, three offerings are made in its honor.
May the fragrance of the flowers bloom forever, may the song of the tides ring out forever, may the dancing flames blaze forever.
May the rhythm of the wind remain free beneath this eternal turning of time.
